subject: Post-call: Model fit & evals — follow-up, benchmarks, and regression next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@retailco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & evals — follow-up, benchmarks, and regression next steps

Hi Sara — great to meet with you and the RetailCo team earlier. Thanks for walking through the priority use cases (product search summarization + product Q&A) and for sharing the eval prompt-set. Quick recap + next steps below.

Recap
- Goals: improve on-answer precision for Q&A and reduce hallucination on price/availability constraints. Latency SLO: 150ms p50 for search-summaries.
- Data we have: RetailCo prompt set v202708 (shared), sample user transcripts, and your product taxonomy.

Preliminary model recommendations
- redwood-instruct-13b (baseline for instruction-tuned quality) — best for dialog/factuality.
- redwood-open-2.7b-quant (cost-optimized) — good candidate for non-critical, high-throughput routes.

Benchmarks & artifacts shared
- Eval summary (attached: eval-summary.csv) — includes per-prompt accuracy, hallucination rate, and latency.
- Drive folder with full benchmarks + prompt sets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/RETAILCO-EVALS-2027

Notable findings from today's quick review
- A small but consistent drop in factual recall on product availability for the latest model snapshot (v1.4) vs v1.3 on a 200-sample slice. See attached eval-summary.csv.
- Reductions concentrated on a subset of prompts that reference SKUs and time-relative language ("in stock this week").

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Allow Redwood SEs to run an expanded regression analysis on your full prompt set (we'll add additional signal windows & stratify by SKU frequency) — ETA 48 hours.
2) If regressions persist, we can 1) pin affected routes to v1.3, or 2) run a targeted hotfix/patch to v1.4. Pinning is fastest.
3) Set up a short (30 min) canary with 10% traffic to v1.3 vs 90% to v1.4 to validate fix before full rollback/pin.

Would you like us to proceed with the expanded analysis? If yes, we will queue it and share a detailed diff and suggested rollback window.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

P.S. CC'd Marcus (SE) and Rishi (CS) who will own technical analysis and ops coordination.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sara Thompson <sara@retailco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & evals — follow-up, benchmarks, and regression next steps

Hi all — quick technical notes from my side after a first-pass on the eval-summary. I've attached a diff archive (diffs-v1.3-v1.4.zip) with example failing inputs and token-level attention that shows where the model is substituting out-of-vocabulary SKU tokens with plausible but incorrect SKUs.

Short summary:
- Aggregate: v1.4 shows a ~6.2% drop in factual-recall F1 on the SKU subset (200-sample slice).
- Latency: 13% improvement p50 for redwood-instruct-13b quantized kernels, but this is not the axis you care about here.
- Likely cause: a tokenizer regression and a changed fallback for low-frequency tokens after the recent tokenizer merge.

Mitigation options (sorted by speed):
A) Pin affected routes to v1.3 — immediate, no model build required.
B) Deploy v1.4 + tokenization patch (hotfix) — requires a rebuild and a 3-5 hour validation window.
C) Canary + selective prefix filtering for SKU-heavy prompts — medium complexity.

If RetailCo wants a quick mitigation, I recommend option A (pin to v1.3) for the SKU-sensitive routes while we validate a tokenization patch. If you approve, we can schedule a pin within the next 2 hours (low-risk) and run the expanded regression analysis in parallel.

Attachment: diffs-v1.3-v1.4.zip (contains per-prompt diffs and tokenization traces)

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: RetailCo Product <pm@retailco.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & evals — follow-up, benchmarks, and regression next steps

Marissa / Marcus — thanks for the quick follow-up and for pulling the initial diffs. We ran a few production checks overnight and confirmed the regressions on our end — several customer-facing queries returned incorrect SKU availability that definitely impacts checkout flows. We've attached a small sample set (samples-failing-prompts.txt) with the failing outputs.

This is high priority for us. Two asks:
1) Can you pin the affected routes to v1.3 immediately (or perform an immediate rollback)? We have a scheduled marketing push tomorrow and need the SKU answers to be correct.
2) Share a proposed timeline for a permanent fix (tokenizer patch or model retune).

If pinning is the fastest option, please proceed and let us know the exact time window — we will coordinate traffic/rate-limit rules on our side if needed.

Thanks —
Sara Thompson
Head of Product, Search | RetailCo
sara.thompson@retailco.com

Attachment: samples-failing-prompts.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@retailco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & evals — follow-up, benchmarks, and regression next steps

Sara — understood, and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as an operational priority. Proposed immediate plan: 

1) Pin affected routes to v1.3 now (low-risk) — target start: 2027-08-23T10:00:00-07:00 (in ~46 minutes). We will:
   - Update routing policy to pin the product-search and sku-answering routes to v1.3.
   - Run smoke tests against your sample set and the provided failing prompts.

2) Run expanded regression analysis (48 hours) and deliver a technical diff + remediation plan (hotfix timeline or model retune).

3) If hotfix is feasible (<6 hours), we'll prioritize that and roll it through a canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Otherwise we'll keep the pin until full validation completes.

Actions I'm taking now:
- Marcus: please prepare the pin deploy and smoke tests.
- Rishi: please schedule an incident bridge and capture SLA-impact notes for our internal escalation path.

Sara — please confirm you want us to proceed with the 10:00 PDT pin window and we'll execute. We'll share the runbook link and the post-pin verification report once complete.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
